report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward news/blog/web-media style content relative to Model A.

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Late-layer concentration: The difference’s L2 norm explodes in mid-to-late layers (L14–L25), consistent with a high-level style/domain shift rather than low-level tokenization effects.
- News/site navigation vocabulary: Repeated top tokens include section headers typical of newspaper sites: “Sports,” “Traffic,” “Fashion,” “Home,” “metropolitan,” plus byline-ish/admin tokens like “spokeswoman,” “chairman,” “Obama,” “politicians,” “journalists,” “billionaire.”
- Blog/platform lexicon dominates positions 2–4 across many late layers: “blogs,” “blogger,” “Blog,” “blogging,” “facebook,” “photo,” “video,” “http.”
- Page/formatting cues: Frequent “ad,” “Mail,” “TV,” “(”, “-”, dates/months (“Mar,” “May”), and many newline/space/punctuation tokens at L23–L25 suggest header/footer/list-like or article-page scaffolding.

Interpretation: Model B’s residual stream differs along a direction that steers outputs toward news/blog/article webpage content and formatting. This supports a domain difference (e.g., additional exposure/fine-tuning on news/blog/web media text) rather than a distinct objective.
